note: Committed summary of genuine Nansen API usage, so a reviewer cloning this repository can verify the buildathon's 1,000-call requirement without access to the local runtime ledger. The full per-call ledger (data/api-usage.json) is gitignored along with the API key.

competition.name: Meridian Buildathon (Build With Nansen API)
competition.requirement: Make 1,000 API calls to prove the Nansen API is genuinely used

attribution.note: The 43-call difference between 952 actually spent in campaign cycles and the 909 the cap ledger recorded has two causes: 3 legacy runs (2026-09-23 to 2026-09-24) stored liveApiCalls but no runReport, so the cap scored them 0; and 2 later runs recorded more than the cumulative ledger advanced, dropping 10 increments to a write race in appendUsage. The race is fixed and covered by test/apiUsage.test.js. The enforcement ledger was deliberately left unmodified.

campaignCap.enforcedAt: send site (src/server/callBudget.js), which never reads the usage ledger
campaignCap.result: Held. The 909 cap was never breached at the point of transmission.

budgetGuard.note: This 1,000 figure is a safety cap inside this repository, not a competition limit. During the final run it failed open when the usage ledger could not be read, permitting 247 calls where 236 remained. The guard now fails closed; see docs/POSTMORTEM.md and test/ledgerFailClosed.test.js.

verification.dryRunResult: 909/909 sent against a fake local Nansen; request 910 never sent; no real API calls
